column4: Pixel-art game character sprites in exactly the same style as the reference image, a mid-1990s Build-engine game: the same coarse pixel size, the same limited palette, the same shading and the same dark outline. A character turnaround model sheet: five full-body views of one and the same person standing too straight, the camera held at his chest in both hands, side by side in a single row, evenly spaced with clear magenta gaps between them, all exactly the same height and scale with the feet on one common baseline near the bottom edge: (1) seen straight from the front, (2) a three-quarter view from the front with the body turned toward the right edge of the image, (3) an exact side profile facing the right edge of the image, (4) a three-quarter view from behind, turned away toward the right edge of the image so the back and the right shoulder show, (5) seen straight from behind, the back of the head and the back of the clothes. Every figure is exactly the man in the reference image, with the same face, body, proportions, clothes and colours: a chubby middle-aged tourist, a green and white trucker cap, black sunglasses, a beige t-shirt with a green mountain and a red sun printed on it, a black film camera on a strap round his neck, a rolled green sleeping mat under his arm, a red and black checked flannel shirt tied round his waist, frayed denim shorts, white socks, brown hiking boots; his smile much too wide with too many small teeth, his sunburn gone grey and peeling in patches. Eerie and unsettling, an enemy in a horror game. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around and between the figures, no ground, no floor line, no shadows, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no frames, no borders, no watermark.

Pixel-art close-up in exactly the style, pixel size, palette and lighting of the reference image: exactly the same man's face filling the frame, the same green and white trucker cap, the same two camera lenses grown into his eye sockets, the same beige t-shirt and camera strap. The only change: no grin at all, his face is slack and dead, the mouth hanging a little open and crooked, grey lips, the jaw loose, a thread of drool, the sunburnt skin gone grey and peeling in patches. Eerie and unsettling, an enemy in a horror game, morbid and never funny. Flat pure magenta #FF00FF background only in the corners, no text.

Pixel-art game character sprite in exactly the same style as the reference image, a mid-1990s Build-engine game: the same coarse pixel size, the same limited palette, the same shading and the same dark outline. One full-body figure: exactly the same man as the reference in the same clothes and colours, the green and white trucker cap, black sunglasses, the beige t-shirt with the mountain print, the camera on its strap, the rolled sleeping mat, the checked flannel shirt round his waist, frayed denim shorts, boots, running at the viewer in a lurching stride, the camera raised in one hand. The only change: no grin, his face slack and expressionless, the mouth hanging open, the head lolling loosely to one side as he runs. Eerie and unsettling, an enemy in a horror game, morbid and never funny. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the figure, no ground, no shadow, no text, no border, no watermark.

Pixel-art texture for a 1990s Build-engine game, seen straight on, filling the whole frame: the weathered wooden door of a small camp cabin at dawn, grey planks and a rusty latch, and pinned to it with a bent nail at eye height a single instant photograph with a white border: a flash photo taken from above in the dark of a person asleep in a camp bed, their face lit harsh white, eyes closed, the blanket pulled up, the room black behind. Chunky pixels, low saturation, gritty and eerie, no text, no border, no watermark.
